# Paths fed to BOTH check-stubs implementations' --classify/-Classify mode, WITH
# the verdict each one must return. The format is exactly what --classify prints:
#
#     source <path>     this file's markers count toward the ratchet
#     skip <path>       this file is not shipped behaviour
#
# EXACTLY ONE SPACE between the verdict and the path. The comparison is a plain
# `diff` against what `--classify` prints, and it prints one space. This header used
# to align the two examples into columns, which is how seventeen rows got added with
# padding that made the fixture disagree with itself.
#
# tests/framework-checks.sh strips the verdict column to build the input, runs
# both implementations, and diffs their output against THIS FILE.
#
# One path per line. Blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored. The
# files do not have to exist -- classification is a decision about the PATH. Paths
# containing spaces do not belong here: `--classify` takes a word list and
# `-Classify` takes a comma-separated string, so neither can carry one. The
# enumeration of such paths is covered by the planted-count check instead.
#
# WHY THE VERDICT IS WRITTEN DOWN. The two implementations were first compared by
# diffing their marker regexes, which are identical and always were; the
# disagreement lived in the file filter next to them. Comparing the two ANSWERS
# fixed that and introduced a subtler version of the same defect: parity is
# agreement, not correctness. Gutting `is_source` in BOTH implementations so that
# nothing at all is classified as source left the suite fully green -- two
# implementations agreeing perfectly about nothing. An expected verdict is the
# only thing neither implementation gets a vote on.
#
# Add the path that disagreed here BEFORE fixing the disagreement.

# --- ordinary source: counted --------------------------------------------
source src/app.ts
source src/Api/Program.cs
source main.go
source lib/util.rb
source Makefile
source src/latest/run.ts
source src/testify-helpers/README.rs
source build-tools/gen.py

# --- `test` as a SUBSTRING is not a test file (G7) ------------------------
# `git mv src/ledger.ts src/latest-ledger.ts` took the count from 1 to 0 on both
# implementations. A rename is not a code review event, so anyone could walk
# through that hole without meaning to.
source src/latest-ledger.ts
source protest.go
source contest.rb
source Greatest.cs
source attestation.ts
source Testing.cs

# --- ...and as a WORD it is, however the language spells it ---------------
skip src/order_test.go
skip src/test_order.py
skip src/OrderTests.cs
skip src/UserSpec.scala
skip src/order-tests.js
skip Test.cs

skip check-stubs.ps1
skip tooling/gate/check-stubs.sh
skip tooling/gate/check-stubs.ps1

# --- the framework's OWN installed tooling is not project source -------------
# Found by the first real v2.2.0 -> v2.3.0 upgrade rehearsal. A fresh multi-repo
# install with ZERO application code baselined at 1, because the word TODO appears
# in a COMMENT inside tooling/ci/gate-ci.sh. Consequence, reproduced: appending one
# explanatory `# TODO:` line to the framework's own CI script made the ratchet FAIL
# on a project whose code had not changed. Every framework release that edits a
# comment in its own tooling would break every consuming project's ratchet.
#
# These are files the framework installs and owns. A marker in them is upstream's
# prose about deferred work, never the project's.
skip gate.sh
skip gate.ps1
skip tooling/ci/gate-ci.sh
skip api/tooling/ci/gate-ci.sh
skip .claude/hooks/guard-installs.sh
skip .claude/hooks/verify-guard.ps1
skip .claude/settings.json
skip .claude/commands/phase-done.md
skip .github/workflows/gate.yml
skip .github/CODEOWNERS
skip azure-pipelines.yml
skip bitbucket-pipelines.yml
# ...but a project file that merely LOOKS like tooling is still source.
source src/gate.ts
source src/tooling/ci/pipeline.ts
source app/github/webhook.go

# --- configuration dotfiles are not code ------------------------------------
# Same rehearsal: `.gitignore` classified as source while README.md did not,
# because is_source is a deny-list and no rule named it. A leading-dot file with no
# further extension is configuration; one WITH a code extension still counts.
skip .gitignore
skip .gitattributes
skip .editorconfig
skip .dockerignore
skip .npmrc
source .eslintrc.js
source .prettierrc.ts

# --- a dotfile with an extension must still reach the extension rule ---------
# The dotfile-config arm and the extension arm lived in the SAME `case`, so a
# dotfile matched `.*)` and the block ended before `*.md`/`*.json`/`*.yml` were ever
# tested. `.foo.md` classified as SOURCE while `README.md` did not. The
# per-platform wrapper filename rule was masking the one instance anybody had
# noticed (.gitlab-ci.yml); these rows cover the shape rather than the instance.
skip .foo.md
skip .bar.json
skip .baz.yaml
skip .notes.txt
skip .data.csv
skip .lock.sum
skip .gitlab-ci.yml
# A dotfile whose extension is NOT excluded stays source -- asserted above as
# `source .eslintrc.js`. It is deliberately not repeated here: this file is compared
# by a plain `diff` against `--classify` output, so a path listed twice with two
# different verdicts makes the fixture contradict itself and the failure names the
# fixture rather than the bug.
